stem: A team wants a specific long-term follow-up claim about procedural pain outcomes, but no explicit supporting text is available; which option best aligns with source rules?

options.text: Infer a standard follow-up plan from usual surgical teaching
Draft the item anyway because follow-up questions are part of the preferred style mix
Use the question style mix as factual justification for the missing content
Do not generate a specific follow-up claim unless explicit supporting text is available
Substitute adult practice principles because they are usually similar

explanation: Do not generate unsupported follow-up claims. When explicit source text is absent, the item should not invent a specific clinical outcome or follow-up statement.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Paediatric Surgery section listed in table of contents

rationale: Unsupported factual claims should not be inferred from general teaching or style guidance.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because usual teaching is external knowledge and not explicit source support.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because preferred style does not override the need for evidence-based content.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because style guidance is not factual justification for missing clinical content.
optionExplanations.D: Correct because a specific follow-up claim should only be generated when explicit supporting text is available.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because adult practice principles are an unsupported extrapolation for this paediatric context.
